name: Tic-Tac-Toe
summary: Tic-tac-toe with large marks, the game that ends the film. WOPR plays perfectly, so the best you can do is a draw.
howToPlay: Tic-tac-toe is not on LIST GAMES (wopr --games shows it under ALSO AVAILABLE). Start it with wopr ttt, or ask WOPR for it by name.
At PLEASE LIST NUMBER OF PLAYERS: type 1 to play WOPR, 2 for two people taking turns at one keyboard, or 0 to let WOPR play itself, as at the end of the film.
With one player you are X and move first. WOPR is O and answers each move with a line such as WOPR: 3.

At YOUR MOVE: type a square from 1 to 9, numbered left to right from the top row, or a column letter and row number from A1 (top left) to C3 (bottom right). A taken square gets CHOOSE AN EMPTY SQUARE, 1 TO 9.
Three in a row wins. A full board with no line is a draw: WINNER: NONE.

controls.does: at the players prompt, play against WOPR
at the players prompt, two players take turns
at the players prompt, WOPR plays itself (the film's ending)
take the top-left square; columns A to C, rows 1 to 3
leave the game and go back to WOPR

tips: WOPR never makes a mistake, so a draw is the best result. Before each move, check whether WOPR has two in a row with the third square empty, and block it.
Open in a corner. The only safe answer is the centre: WOPR always finds it, but a friend playing O in a two-player game often does not.
WOPR picks at random among its best moves, so games differ even though it never loses. With a seed (wopr ttt -s 7) it makes the same choices every time, which helps you study a line of play.
Try 0 players to see what WOPR learns from playing itself.

screenshots.caption: The empty board shows each square's number. YOU are X and WOPR is O.
After 5, WOPR takes 3; a second 3 is refused (CHOOSE AN EMPTY SQUARE, 1 TO 9.), A1 takes the top left, and WOPR blocks the diagonal with 9, its last mark underlined.
The full board is a draw: WINNER: NONE, then SHALL WE PLAY ANOTHER GAME?
